evaluation.lede: Wrong on too many calls, and no ticket structure fixes a bad read. The legs get fixed first.
paragraphs: Here is my honest read of how we attacked PHI @ CHI. Final: PHI 7 - 27 CHI. We graded 22 unique predictions, 10 passed (45%), and 0 of 16 tickets cashed (0%), for -$80 on $80 staked. We were right on fewer than half of the individual calls, so this one is partly a prediction problem, and no ticket structure fixes a read that is wrong. The fixes below start with which legs we trust. 2 of the 16 losing tickets died by exactly one leg, which is the cost of asking every ticket to be perfect.

The damage came from contagion. D'Andre Swift over 0.5 anytime TD finished at 0 against a 0.5 line and sat on 10 tickets, the only miss on 1 of them. One bad number, many dead tickets. D'Andre Swift failed in more than one prop line, 11 ticket slots in total, which is the same mistake in a different font.

Length is the clearest signal. Tickets of three legs or fewer cashed 0 of 8; tickets of four or more cashed 0 of 8. Every extra leg multiplies the chance of one dead leg, and we keep paying for payout we rarely collect. Trimming every ticket to its three most likely legs would have saved 0 losing tickets on the same predictions.

Receiving yardage went 3 for 4 (75%). Yardage props are the noisiest thing on the board, so they belong with the receivers who dominate targets, not with whoever is third in the pecking order. A WR3 at four targets a game cannot carry a ticket, and I do not want him as the load-bearing leg again.

Here is what has to change for the numbers to turn around. One: a player and a prop appear once. If he is already on a card, use a different market (receptions, rushing, or rushing plus receiving yards) and never the same prop on every ticket. Crazy Horse is the only exception. Two: three legs and go home, with at most one long ticket a night. Three: legs go to players who are essential to their offense and see the targets or the carries. Four: build around the shape that wins most often. Replayed on 15 games of graded predictions, 1 passing + 1 rushing + 1 receiving, all at SAFE (-15%) lines cashed 48% of 450 tickets. Touchdown legs are back, but only for essential players. They scored in 26% of games this season versus 13% for everyone else, so they get a seat, not the whole card.

For the season we are 20 and 65 on tickets (24%) and 77 and 57 on legs (57%). The legs are fine. The tickets are where we are bleeding, which is why every rule above is about how the legs are combined.
